question: Whether a raider keeps a convoy ship as its target between rounds.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::PickTarget
addresses.signature: CSubUnit* __thiscall CSubUnit::PickTarget(CSubUnit* attacker, CNavalCombatant* side, CCombatant* other)
addresses.comment: **Who a ship shoots at this hour.** `p = (definition.positioning + side.positioning) * 100 * (1 + the country's naval_positioning_bonus, the technology key targeting_chance)`, a whole number, halved at night for the second test. A remembered target (+0xB8/+0xBC) that still exists is forgotten on `Random() % 50 > p + 10`, and at night on a further `Random() % 100 > 80`; one of another country is kept only while its fleet is on the other side, and one of the ship's own country is kept a quarter of the time. With none: `Random() % 80 > p` means the ship has lost the enemy - no target, or with `Random() % 100 < 7 - the skill of the side's highest ranked leader` (CCombatant::GetHighestRankedLeader of its own side, where his slot 8 answers yes) **one of its own side's ships** (the walk does not stop at the ship drawn and ends on the last one of the side). Otherwise CNavalCombatant::CollectTargets fills the side's list with the enemy ships in reach, and the target is a random one of them, or - on `Random() % 100 <= CSubUnit::TargetingSkill / 10` - CNavalCombatant::PickBestTarget's. The pick is remembered. So positioning buys a ship a target at all, and keeps the one it has. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4. **How the remembered target is found** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 119): the pair at +0xB8/+0xBC, written from the target's +8/+0xC when a pick is kept (0x167778), is looked up through one of two registries chosen by the pair's first word against 0x1268 (0x23D57F0 or 0x23D57F4, the call at 0x1676D1); where nothing answers, the fresh pick follows. A convoy raid's throwaway fleet is not found there - inferred from a recording of July 1941, where Italy's 3rd Navy raiding a French convoy picks afresh in every one of the five rounds - so a raider never keeps a convoy ship.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x1675D0-0x1677B3 read live 2026-11-18; recording wr15 tick 60807908, draws 445-447 of the hour (PickTarget +0x1F0, +0x2CE, +0x2FB) in round two as in round one. Wrong if a raider is seen keeping a convoy ship between rounds.
addresses.revises: comment - the remembered target's lookup, and the raid's convoy never found by it
